heading: Purpose
guidance: Why the policy exists and what it is intended to achieve for the organization.

heading: Definitions
guidance: A table of the specialist terms this policy uses, with plain definitions. Include only terms the policy actually uses. Abbreviations are expanded in the Abbreviations section, so do not repeat them here; define the full term instead when it needs explaining.

heading: Abbreviations
guidance: One table with exactly two columns, "Abbreviation" and "Full Form / Description", listing the abbreviations this policy itself uses (for example MFA, RBAC, ISMS), one per row, each once, with its accurate full form in this policy's context. List only abbreviations that appear in the other sections. Do not invent abbreviations for the organization, and do not list ordinary terms here; those belong in Definitions. If the policy uses no abbreviations, write a single sentence saying so instead of a table.

heading: Scope
guidance: Who and what the policy applies to: roles, departments, systems, data, locations and third parties named in the analysis. State anything explicitly out of scope if the documents say so.

heading: Policy Objectives and Principles
guidance: One combined section of subject-specific objectives and guiding principles. Do not create separate Objectives or Principles sections. Avoid general ISMS goals in specialist documents.

heading: Policy Principles
guidance: The guiding principles behind the detailed requirements.

heading: Roles and Responsibilities
guidance: A table with the columns "Role / Department", "Responsibilities" and "Basis" (Documented or Proposed). Name role titles, departments, teams or designations only, such as IT Manager, Information Security Team or Department Heads. Never write the name of an individual person: where the documents name a person, give the role or department that person holds if the documents state it, and otherwise use a placeholder for the role. Use the roles the documents establish; label any role or duty you introduce as Proposed.

heading: Policy Requirements
guidance: The binding requirements, as statements blocks grouped under topic subheadings. Convert the identified requirements into clear, testable statements and add proposed statements for significant risks and gaps. Reference supporting finding ids. Assign duties to roles, never to named individuals.

heading: Procedures and Implementation Guidelines
guidance: Practical guidance on putting the requirements into effect: steps, sequencing and which role acts, drawing on the recommended controls and suggested actions.

heading: Risk Management and Security Controls
guidance: Identify risks specific to this document, with scenario, consequence, responsible role, treatment and review. Use only relevant evidence. If no subject-specific risk is evidenced, state proposed risk assessment requirements and missing inputs rather than listing unrelated ISMS risks.

heading: Monitoring and Compliance
guidance: How adherence to the policy is monitored, measured and reported, and the consequences of non-compliance. Mention open gaps that must be tracked to closure.

heading: Incident Reporting and Escalation
guidance: How suspected breaches of this policy or related security incidents are reported and escalated, including time limits and the roles or contact points if the documents give them.

heading: Exceptions and Approval Process
guidance: How exceptions to the policy are requested, risk-assessed, approved, time-limited and recorded, and which role approves them.

heading: Review and Maintenance
guidance: How often the policy is reviewed, what triggers an out-of-cycle review, and which role maintains it.

heading: References
guidance: The source documents this policy was drafted from, and any standards, laws or internal documents that those sources themselves cite. Do not add standards or laws the sources do not mention.

heading: Executive Summary
guidance: No longer part of a policy. It is listed here so that the application recognises it in policies saved by earlier versions and in model output, and leaves it out of every new version.
